Module ID: MOD-DE01-FOUNDATION-01. Content version: 2.0. Review: NEEDS_EXPERT_REVIEW.

## Learning objective

This revised learning unit focuses on **create data models**. Other activities support that single objective; they are not additional learning outcomes. This is a locally authored lesson/lab scaffold pending expert content, sandbox and assessment approval.


## Read and prepare

Use [the retained introduction and official references](MOD-DE01-FOUNDATION-01.md) for background. The original file is historical reference, not a second required completion or the current task scope.

Create an entity model from supplied requirements; verify keys and relationships against sample records.

Follow a supplied example, make one controlled change and verify the result.

Use the supplied small warehouse/load scaffold only to check that the model preserves keys and grain. Record a concise data dictionary for the model. A full warehouse implementation is not a second main objective.

## Skill and completion contract

This edition teaches only **MS-DE01 — create data models**. Complete all lessons to meet the learning prerequisite for this Skill assessment. Other approved Modules for the same Skill remain optional. Completion is not an assessment result or mastery decision.

Module ID: MOD-ARC02-INTERMEDIATE-01. Content version: 2.0. Review: NEEDS_EXPERT_REVIEW.

## Purpose and scenario

Practice **Compare architecture alternatives** using a booking service with API, storage and external notification boundaries. This locally authored review package is a scaffold for expert lesson/lab authoring, not a complete approved course.

## Teaching focus and difficulty


## Read and prepare

Read [the retained source-linked introduction](MOD-ARC02-FOUNDATION-01.md) for terminology and references. It is a reference, not a compulsory module completion. Review the supplied scenario, inputs and expected outputs with the instructor. For real use, experts must provide and approve the actual sandbox assets, worked examples and task/rubric configuration.

## Practice task

Compare feasible designs against agreed quality, cost and risk criteria.

Implement a variant independently from the stated requirements. Diagnose one injected failure and justify the correction with before/after checks.

## Supporting task

Create a short decision record explaining assumptions and how the primary design was checked. The supporting activity develops Document and explain architecture decisions; review its evidence separately from the primary result.

## Incidental context

A repository snapshot is provided as context; source-control operations are not taught or assessed here. Merely using that context does not close a gap for MS-CORE02.

## Checks and evidence

Submit the learning artifact, stated assumptions, expected-versus-observed checks and one limitation. Include evidence for the supporting activity. For ADVANCED difficulty, add the alternative comparison, failure analysis and recovery checks; for INTERMEDIATE, include diagnosis and correction; for FOUNDATION, retain the worked-example checklist and changed-input result. No evidence or attainment decision is claimed for incidental context.

## Readiness and assessment boundary

Skill prerequisite edges determine readiness; supporting/incidental links do not create new prerequisites. An approved external task/rubric and compatible learner evidence are required to confirm readiness or attainment. Difficulty is an expert authoring category, not a numeric score threshold, role-Level shortcut, or expected mastery increase. Completion never automatically passes any skill.

## Skill and completion contract

This edition teaches only **MS-ARC02 — Compare architecture alternatives**. Complete all lessons to meet the learning prerequisite for this Skill assessment. Other approved Modules for the same Skill remain optional. Completion is not an assessment result or mastery decision.

Practice **Implement data extraction** at advanced level. This is pre-published development sample content; it is not a human-reviewed course.

Extract records from two supplied paginated data files. Preserve stable keys, record a checkpoint and show how rerunning the extraction avoids duplicates.

Keep the small learning artifact, expected-versus-observed checks and a short explanation of your decisions. Use synthetic inputs and record any assumptions.

Complete the lesson, then take the configured Skill assessment for MS_DE10_ADVANCED. Reading or marking the module complete does not award official achievement; the assessment and applicable prerequisite rules still apply.

A repository snapshot is provided as context; source-control operations are not taught or assessed here. Merely using that context does not close a gap for MS-CORE02.

## Checks and evidence

Submit the learning artifact, stated assumptions, expected-versus-observed checks and one limitation. Include evidence for the supporting activity. For ADVANCED difficulty, add the alternative comparison, failure analysis and recovery checks; for INTERMEDIATE, include diagnosis and correction; for FOUNDATION, retain the worked-example checklist and changed-input result. No evidence or attainment decision is claimed for incidental context.

## Readiness and assessment boundary

Skill prerequisite edges determine readiness; supporting/incidental links do not create new prerequisites. An approved external task/rubric and compatible learner evidence are required to confirm readiness or attainment. Difficulty is an expert authoring category, not a numeric score threshold, role-Level shortcut, or expected mastery increase. Completion never automatically passes any skill.

## Skill and completion contract

This edition teaches only **MS-SEC10 — Maintain security policy procedures**. Complete all lessons to meet the learning prerequisite for this Skill assessment. Other approved Modules for the same Skill remain optional. Completion is not an assessment result or mastery decision.
